items.author: Global Voices Eurasia
items.title: Letter from a jailed Azerbaijani political prisoner reveals deadly consequences of silence
items.summary: Bahruz Samadov: “The selective attitude to the human rights issues and turning the blind eye to our suffering endangers the democratic security of the US itself, not to mention its international image.”

items.author: Daria Dergacheva
items.title: While Russia tries to manipulate information, local civil society is teaching Armenians media literacy
items.summary: With the proliferation of generative AI, disinformation and propaganda campaigns have become increasingly sophisticated. Armenia’s experience shows how they operate in a country moving away from its longstanding reliance on Russia.

items.author: Janine Mendes-Franco
items.title: Trinbagonian Jason Jones wins landmark Privy Council judgement deeming ‘buggery laws’ unconstitutional
items.summary: After a decade-long legal battle, the Privy Council has overturned a 2025 Court of Appeal decision to keep Trinidad and Tobago’s colonial-era “buggery law” on the books.

items.author: Gina Yauri
items.title: Ecuadorian youth unite against neoliberal models and state violence
items.summary: Thousands of Ecuadorian students have taken to the streets to reject President Noboa’s temporary job plans, demanding permanent solutions for public healthcare, education funding, and rising insecurity.

items.author: Sandra Tuombouh
items.title: Can regenerative school gardens strengthen food security in Cameroon?
items.summary: Students in Cameroon’s North West Region are managing school gardens and growing food using regenerative practices such as minimal tillage, composting, organic manure and fruit-tree grafting.

items.author: Guest Contributor
items.title: Justice is the infrastructure the world keeps forgetting
items.summary: Physical infrastructure cannot deliver its promised benefits when the institutions and mechanisms for resolving grievances are inaccessible, ineffective or distrusted.

items.author: Laura
items.title: Restoring social media access comes at a cost in Gabon
items.summary: After more than eight months, Gabon has restored its social media access. But it has come at a cost.

items.author: Nurbek Bekmurzaev
items.title: In Ukraine, youth are finding their voices in the digital democracy
items.summary: We saw a gap: young people were consuming information and even participating online, but without media literacy, digital security awareness, or confidence that their voice could shape anything.

items.author: Global Voices East Asia
items.title: Ex-lawmaker sentenced to 12.5 years in prison in closed-door trial in Macau
items.summary: Macau recorded its first conviction under the city’s national security law on November 6, 2026, sentencing 69-year-old former lawmaker Au Kam San to 12.5 years in prison. Observers call it an “unfair” “sham trial”

items.author: Jude Pierre Louis
items.title: From a quiet life to the terror of armed gangs: The story of Haiti’s Kenscoff district
items.summary: After the first of two deadly gang attacks this year, the Kenscoff community, like many other regions in the country, turned from peaceful living to being held to ransom.
